title: What’s new in OpenText Content Aviator
summary: Get the latest news and updates related to OpenText Content Aviator Cloud Editions and the impact of GenAI content management.
body_text: OpenText™ Content Aviator puts an AI content assistant into the hands of business users: one that can act on that content, not just search and summarize content in place. Built on a fully governed, secure foundation, Content Aviator brings secure information management for AI to every user and process. It is available across all OpenText Content Cloud platforms for content management and archiving. July 2026: What’s new in OpenText Content Aviator 26.2 The 26.2 release of Content Aviator brings a major new set of capabilities and a strong governance foundation for agentic AI . Safety and AI governance are critical to the success of engaging agentic AI in your overall strategies. The combination of agents, new skills, and process-centric knowledge graphs gives your teams what they need to decide, act, and transact safely on your content. Content Aviator 26.2 puts our vision into practice: governed content now connects to more of the AI systems your teams already use. It goes beyond search and summary to take intelligent action on your content. It becomes the secure, agentic foundation for accessing your information, either directly or through integrations with Microsoft Copilot, Salesforce Agentforce, and Google Gemini Enterprise, providing governance and trust your users can depend on. Here’s what’s new in 26.2. Agentic AI opens up a new level of AI content management Content Aviator expands well beyond search, summary and draft to act on your content. With OpenText Content Management 26.2, here are just a few things you can achieve now with Content Aviator and agentic AI: Ground your work on the right content through the knowledge graph: Content Aviator orients your work to what you’re working on intelligently, giving a 360-degree view of the most up-to-date information available at any time. Through the knowledge graph, OpenText Content Aviator understands relationships across a network of connected workspaces Put agentic AI to work within your processes with business workspace management: Create new workspaces, update metadata, and create relationships between workspaces. Manage documents and records with ease: Rename, move, copy and change permissions on documents. Records management: Classify documents, set legal holds, and apply markings or security clearances. User agent: Look up users, favorite items, and review recently accessed documents. Generate templated, finished documents, not just drafts: The document generation agent lets users define templates for common business documents and generate a completed document from a single natural-language request; no manual searching or setup required. New document generation agent powered by OpenText Content Aviator Kickoff new workflows: Define prescribed workflows and initiate them from Content Aviator. The throughline across all of it: less time hunting for information, more time acting on it. Integrate Content Aviator with leading AI systems for the ultimate context and control Integrating with the AI systems your organization uses gives users the flexibility to stay “in the zone” and get work done efficiently, while benefiting from safe access to your organization’s critical content when and where they need it. Earlier, we introduced AI integration with Microsoft Copilot and Salesforce Agentforce . Now, with Google Gemini Enterprise (available with OpenText Core Content Management 26.2), integration gives teams using Gemini Enterprise and Google Workspace direct access to Content Aviator, ensuring proper security permissions and important AI governance controls are applied during AI use on their critical content. Users tap into Content Aviator directly from the Gemini chat interface, keeping content safe beyond policy-driven permissions enforced on every response. Access OpenText Content Aviator directly inside the Gemini chat interface Microsoft Copilot: Inside Microsoft Copilot , users can now see inline citations pointing directly to source documents in OpenText Document Management platforms, a fast way to validate information and locate the business workspace it came from, without ever leaving Copilot. Salesforce Agentforce: And in OpenText Core Content Management for Salesforce 26.2, users can now open business workspaces directly inside Salesforce Agentforce using natural language. Content Aviator identifies and opens the correct workspace without having to navigate away from their train of thought. AI content assistance in the flow of work without switching apps OpenText Documentum Content Management 26.2 brings new flexibility for Content Aviator users Several key improvements are coming to Content Aviator users with OpenText Documentum Content Management: AI-driven natural language search: Content Aviator now drives a natural language search, making complex search simple and combining keyword precision with semantic understanding. Mobile app support: OpenText Documentum Content Management 26.2 now includes Content Aviator within the mobile app for AI content assistance on the go. Expanded deployment flexibility for deploying OpenText Content Aviator with OpenText Information Archive OpenText Information Archive 26.2 extends OpenText Content Aviator’s reach with support for more hyperscalers, models and hybrid deployment scenarios, built for organizations with complex environments. January 2026: What’s new in OpenText Content Aviator 26.1 OpenText Content Aviator is now available from Microsoft Copilot OpenText Content Aviator is now available as a Microsoft Copilot agent, bringing trusted, AI powered content intelligence directly into Microsoft 365. By enabling the OpenText Content Aviator agent from the Microsoft Agent Store, users can select it as their Copilot agent source and converse with OpenText Content Aviator using natural language to search for information, uncover key facts, and generate insights directly from content stored in OpenText Core Content Management, OpenText Content Management, and OpenText Documentum Content Management. This AI-to-AI integration allows users working in Microsoft Word, Excel, and PowerPoint to access governed, context-rich enterprise content without leaving the app. The result is faster research, more informed drafting, and greater productivity—while maintaining the security, permissions, and compliance controls enterprises expect from OpenText content management. Learn more about the OpenText Content Aviator agent in the Microsoft Agent Store . OpenText Content Aviator is accessible from Microsoft Copilot. Upgrade to GPT 5 model on Microsoft Azure OpenText Content Aviator now gives customers access to OpenAI GPT 5 model when deployed on Microsoft Azure. Off-cloud deployments now support the hyperscaler-hosted model With 26.1, customers connect OpenText Content Aviator 26.1 to a hyperscaler-hosted model, giving customers complete control over their environment, end to end, but supporting the efficiency and cost management of a hyperscaler-hosted model. November 2025: What’s new in OpenText Content Aviator CE 25.4 Deploy OpenText Content Aviator off-cloud in your own data center with Meta LLM OpenText Content Aviator CE 25.4 introduces a new off-cloud deployment option, giving organizations the ability to use GenAI-powered content management while meeting strict data residency and compliance requirements. Off-cloud customers of OpenText Content Management and OpenText Documentum Content Management can now deploy OpenText Content Aviator alongside OpenText Aviator Model Services using a fully packaged, production-ready installer. This deployment approach provides everything IT teams need to run GenAI safely, predictably, and securely in highly regulated environments. OpenText Content Aviator now available on Microsoft Azure with OpenAI LLM OpenText Content Aviator CE 25.4 can also be deployed natively on Microsoft Azure using the OpenAI frontier model. By purchasing through the Microsoft Azure Marketplace , customers gain expanded options for technical integration, compliance alignment, and data governance while being supported by a single vendor relationship and a unified SLA. This arrangement also helps organizations maximize their existing Azure commitments with AI-powered content management. Bring key metadata into the conversation This release further improves answer quality through metadata enrichment. OpenText Content Aviator can now retrieve and use metadata from connected business applications to enhance contextual understanding and support queries where key information resides in metadata fields. Direct LLM Access API enables custom applications App developers gain access to a new Direct LLM Access API, enabling them to add basic LLM-driven capabilities directly into their applications. This API reduces reliance and uncertainty around using Chat API for simple, repeatable tasks such as generating document summaries. August 2025: What’s new in OpenText Content Aviator CE 25.3 OpenText Content Aviator: smarter answers, richer visuals OpenText Content Aviator continues to evolve as the embedded AI content assistant inside OpenText Content Management: See your data differently. Aviator can now generate charts such as bar, line, and pie directly in the chat panel, turning complex information into quick, clear visuals without leaving the platform. Better results with tables. Improved table handling provides more context, producing more accurate answers when your content is structured in rows and columns. Choose your AI engine. In addition to GCP and AWS, customers can now deploy Aviator on Azure OpenAI, expanding compliance and regional hosting options. Together, these advances reduce the friction of finding, interpreting, and presenting information, helping knowledge workers make better decisions in less time. April 2025: What’s new in OpenText Content Aviator CE 25.2 OpenText Content Aviator now available on Amazon AWS with Amazon Nova LLM OpenText Content Aviator expands deployment and model flexibility with added support for the Amazon Nova foundation model on Amazon AWS, giving customers additional deployment options. Customers can take advantage of existing cloud investments while meeting regional, compliance, and operational requirements. March 2025: What’s new in OpenText Content Aviator CE 25.1 Announcing Salesforce Agentforce integration We’re excited to announce the availability of our first phase of AI-to-AI integration between OpenText Content Aviator and Salesforce Agentforce. This new integration available for OpenText Content Management CE 25.1 empowers Sales and Customer Service teams with AI-driven enhanced actionable insights to boost productivity and accelerate processes. It enables users to: Discover relevant information fast and easy : Find, summarize, and translate business workspace content, directly within Agentforce. For example, a Sales rep can summarize customer buying trends and upsell products that resonate or a Customer Service agent can easily summarize and resolve a claim. Seamlessly update your Salesforce information with OpenText Content Aviator insights using AI-to-AI integration, reducing manual entry and errors. Interact with customers more intelligently : Write personalized email responses in OpenText Content Aviator and send from Agentforce. With this integration between Agentforce and OpenText Content Aviator, sales teams gain content-driven insights to close deals faster; Customer Service responds more accurately and personally to retain customers; and claims are processed and resolved more efficiently. Find it on Salesforce AppExchange and on the just announced Salesforce AgentExhange marketplace. Integrate OpenText Content Aviator actionable insights, directly in Salesforce Agentforce . November 2024: What’s new in OpenText Content Aviator CE 24.4 OpenText Content Aviator is now integrated with OpenText™ Information Archive to revolutionize how IT data managers interact with legacy content and archived data. Through OpenText Content Aviator’s intuitive LLM-powered chat interface, users can easily access, retrieve, and summarize archived data using natural language. The integration of OpenText Content Aviator with OpenText Information Archive provides rapid insights to unfamiliar archived content, greatly enhancing productivity while assuring sensitive and proprietary information remains secure and adheres to organizational security protocols. OpenText Content Aviator enables smarter, faster, and safeguarded data retrieval from archived systems , making it an indispensable part of the end-user experience when accessing vast amounts of legacy content. OpenText is also pleased to announce the availability of a new 30-day free trial that allows customers to experience the power of OpenText Content Aviator with OpenText Content Management (Extended ECM). Customers receive their own dedicated, OpenText Content Aviator-enabled business workspace to upload their own sample documents specific to their own use cases in this completely self-service experience. Try OpenText Content Aviator today! July 2024: What’s new in OpenText Content Aviator CE 24.3 Customers using OpenText Content Management (Extended ECM) CE 24.1 and later on-premises can now deploy OpenText Content Aviator by accessing it through the OpenText Content Cloud in a hybrid configuration. This means no content must be migrated, but Aviator-related data and AI queries will use the cloud. OpenText Content Aviator is currently available on Google Cloud, but future 2025 releases will support Amazon Web Services and Microsoft Azure cloud configurations. OpenText is also pleased to announce the availability of a new interactive demo showcasing the power of OpenText Content Aviator with Extended ECM. Customers can sign up for this risk-free demo and try OpenText Content Aviator with pre-built, out-of-the-box scenarios for Insurance, Real Estate and HR. This interactive experience allows customers to get started with OpenText Content Aviator immediately with the freedom and flexibility to ask their own questions and try all the latest features of OpenText Content Aviator such as summaries, translation, content generation and more, all at their own pace. Additional scenarios and new features will be added to the interactive demo in future releases. October 2023: Introducing OpenText Content Aviator Transform user productivity with an AI-powered intelligent assistant OpenText is excited to introduce OpenText™ Content Aviator, an AI-powered intelligent assistant now available for OpenText Core Content (CE 24.1 release), Extended ECM (CE 24.2 release) and Documentum (CE 24.3 release) customers. OpenText Content Aviator empowers business users with AI content management and the ability to leverage an interactive chat interface and conversational search to quickly discover content, summarize or translate a document or workspace, and draft content such as emails. By quickly providing relevant answers to natural language questions, OpenText Content Aviator eliminates tedious, manual tasks to help you get work done – faster.

title: Alight expands AI collaboration with IBM to advance benefits administration and employee experiences
summary: Strategic collaboration leverages IBM agentic AI and AI Governance capabilities with Alight’s data and expertise to deliver enhanced employer insights and employee experiences across Alight’s platform and solutions with Agentic AI
body_text: Alight, Inc. (NYSE: ALIT or the “Company”), a leading cloud-based human capital and technology-enabled services provider, today announced an expanded, multi-year collaboration to deploy IBM watsonx into Alight's offerings to transform the employee benefits experience and optimize enterprise operations. This collaboration further advances Alight’s digital transformation and aims to equip clients with AI-powered tools that deliver hyper-personalized benefits support for employees through the responsible use of AI. As part of the collaboration, Alight and IBM are creating a virtual AI innovation lab to accelerate the reengineering of business processes, rapidly prototype new AI solutions, and foster an environment for continuous co-innovation. The lab will bring together specialists from both organizations along with Alight clients to identify and test potential AI use cases, optimize benefit guidance such as leave of absence support, and create new capabilities tailored to client needs. Initial prototypes from the existing collaboration centering on the Alight Worklife AI Assistant experience have shown potential to increase employee productivity by over 90% underscoring the potential impact of AI-driven innovation as the work moves toward full-scale deployment. Pilots are scheduled for early 2026, with broader rollout expected in the first half of 2026. “This collaboration with IBM represents a pivotal moment in delivering high-tech innovation with human touch across our platform,” said Dave Guilmette, Chief Executive Officer at Alight. “By embedding IBM watsonx enterprise AI throughout our portfolio of solutions, as well as within Alight Worklife®, we are transforming how employers assess and measure the impact of their offerings and how employees experience their benefits.” At the core of the collaboration is IBM watsonx Orchestrate, a product offering more than 500 tools and customizable, domain-specific agents from IBM and its partners. Alight will leverage watsonx Orchestrate to enable seamless automation and information flow across Alight’s internal systems, applications, and AI agents. This orchestration will aim to eliminate silos and accelerate the delivery of new capabilities across Alight’s enterprise data fabric. This work will include leveraging the watsonx Orchestrate Agent Catalog—a central marketplace launched in May that simplifies discovery, deployment and enhancements of enterprise agents from IBM, its partners, and custom builds. “We’re excited to be working with Alight to create AI-powered human capital solutions that will benefit many of the world’s largest organizations and their employees,” said Adam Lawrence, General Manager, IBM Americas. “Through our AI innovation lab, we’re prototyping new solutions and deploying IBM watsonx Orchestrate AI agents and a comprehensive enterprise agentic AI architecture to enhance the employee benefits experience. Together with Alight, we can look beyond automating tasks to help optimize enterprise operations and support continuous innovation.” Four strategic domains of innovation Alight and IBM will collaborate across four high-impact use case domains, underpinned by enterprise-grade governance and AI orchestration: Embedding watsonx across Alight Worklife – to power AI-enabled personalized chat and task automation experiences across Alight’s benefits administration, health navigation, wealth, wellbeing, and leaves management solutions. AI-enabled benefits administration modernization – Streamlining data models to reduce complexity and accelerate onboarding and time to value. Automated configuration and insights extraction will enhance decision-making for employers. Enhancing the Alight colleague experience – Applying AI to automate repetitive HR and IT tasks and enhance self-service tools for Alight’s workforce, mirroring IBM’s own “Client Zero” transformation that is expected to help it achieve more than $4 billion in productivity savings by the end of this year. These efficiencies in turn enhance the Alight client experience. Advancing delivery and productivity – Leveraging generative and agentic AI to transform workflows and business processes to accelerate client implementation, improve employer satisfaction, and increased employee benefits utilization through enhanced experiences. To promote transparency, responsibility, accountability and ethical AI, the collaboration will also leverage IBM watsonx.governance, which provides comprehensive oversight, monitoring, and compliance controls across AI deployments. This includes lifecycle management, fairness and bias evaluation, regulatory mapping, and audit trails—reinforcing Alight’s own ongoing commitment to responsible AI.

title: Florida State University Game Day Outfits - How to Dress like a Seminole
summary: Florida State game day is not the time to blend in. You’re in Tallahassee, the energy is loud, the garnet and gold is everywhere, and your outfit needs to keep up.The best Florida State game day outfit feels easy, confident, and a little too good to be accidental. You’re not trying too hard. You just know how to dress
body_text: Florida State game day is not the time to blend in. You’re in Tallahassee, the energy is loud, the garnet and gold is everywhere, and your outfit needs to keep up. The best Florida State game day outfit feels easy, confident, and a little too good to be accidental. You’re not trying too hard. You just know how to dress for your team. Whether you’re heading to a tailgate, walking around campus, or making your way into Doak Campbell Stadium, your look should be cute enough for photos, comfortable enough for the whole day, and spirited enough that everyone knows who you’re cheering for. Start With Garnet and Gold When in doubt, start with the colors. Garnet and gold do most of the work, so you don’t need to overthink it. A Florida State crop top with denim shorts? Always works. A baby tee with a mini skirt? Very game day. An oversized crewneck with biker shorts? Effortless, but still cute. The point is to look like you planned the outfit without making it look like the outfit planned you. FSU game day style should feel cool, easy, and confident. Think pieces you would actually wear outside of game day, just with a Seminoles upgrade. What to Wear to a Florida State Football Game For a Florida State football game, your outfit has to be ready for a lot: tailgating, walking, standing, sweating, cheering, and probably taking photos before you even make it to the stadium. For early-season games, keep it light. Tallahassee gets hot, so this is where crop tops, fitted tanks, baby tees, tube tops, and shorts make the most sense. Pair them with sneakers, cowboy boots, or flat boots so you can actually last all day. For night games or cooler weather, add a layer that still looks intentional. A cropped sweatshirt, oversized Florida State crewneck, varsity jacket, or zip-up gives you that “I just threw this on” look, even though it obviously works. Easy FSU Game Day Outfit Ideas A strong game day closet starts with pieces you can style more than one way. The goal is to have a few Georgia staples that work for tailgates, stadium seating, post-game plans downtown, and every photo in between. FSU Tailgate Outfits for Hot Weather Tallahassee heat is real, so your tailgate outfit needs to be cute without being complicated. This is not the day for heavy layers or shoes you have to think about. Shorts are the safest move. Foldover shorts , gingham shorts , or basketball shorts all look good with a Florida State crop top, tank, or baby tee. A mini skirt also works if you want something a little more feminine but still easy to move in. Simple, clean, and very garnet-and-gold coded. For when you want to give Adam Sandler in a sporty, chic way. Accessories are where you make it feel styled. Gold hoops, sunglasses, a clear bag, and cute sneakers can take a simple FSU outfit and make it feel intentional. Cute Florida State Outfit Ideas That Don’t Try Too Hard The best Florida State University game day outfits are the ones that feel natural. You want to look put together, not like you spent three hours trying to create a “game day look.” Try a garnet jersey with white shorts. Wear a Florida State baby tee with a denim mini skirt. Throw an oversized crewneck over biker shorts. The outfit should say you’re here for the Seminoles, but you also know what you’re doing. What Shoes to Wear on FSU Game Day Shoes matter. You’ll be walking, standing, and probably pretending your feet don’t hurt by the fourth quarter, so choose wisely. White sneakers are always the easiest option. They go with almost every Florida State game day outfit and can handle a full day. Cowboy boots are also a game day favorite, especially with shorts, skirts, or dresses. Flat boots work if you want something that feels a little more styled. Skip anything uncomfortable. Looking cute is the point, but surviving the day is also pretty important. What to Wear for a Cooler Florida State Game Even in Florida, some games get cooler, especially later in the season or at night. That’s when layers make the outfit. An oversized Florida State crewneck is always a good call. Start with a tank or baby tee underneath, then add the layer when the sun goes down. Easy. Florida State Game Day Outfit Checklist Before you head out, make sure your look can actually handle the day: A breathable, cute top Comfortable shorts, a skirt, skort, or biker shorts Shoes you can walk in A clear stadium bag Sunglasses for daytime games A layer for night games Garnet, gold, or something that says Seminoles without screaming it Final Thoughts Dressing for Florida State game day is all about looking good without making it a whole production. You want an outfit that feels confident, easy, and ready for whatever the day turns into. Tailgate first. Cheer loud. Look cute. Repeat. Whether you’re at Doak Campbell Stadium, walking through campus, or heading out after the game, the best FSU game day outfit is the one that makes you feel like the main character without acting like one.

title: Back to the Classroom: How to Relaunch Your Teaching Career After a Break
summary: Practical tips to help former teachers confidently return to the classroom after a career break.
body_text: ‍ Did you step away from teaching for a while, but now hear the classroom calling you back? Returning to teaching after a break can be challenging, but it’s manageable with the right approach. Here’s a quick guide to help you get started. Update Your Credentials Start with the most important thing: your teaching license. Visit the website for your state’s Department of Education to see what is currently required to teach in your subject area. If your credential is expired or no longer acceptable, prioritize completing the requirements needed to get back into compliance. Maybe your credentials remain active, but you’re feeling rusty about aspects of teaching like lesson planning or educational technology. Consider enrolling in professional development or seeking out free online resources to help you brush up. If you’re reconsidering what subject you want to teach and are in a position to pursue an additional endorsement, high-demand subjects like Special Education, English as a Second Language or a STEM subject can increase your chances of getting hired. Update Your Resume Make sure your resume is well-crafted and current, including the time you’ve been off – which we’ll cover next. If you completed any training, professional development, coursework or volunteer work that isn’t captured, add it there now. Depending how long you’ve been away, you may also consider updating the language in your resume to reflect current trends. For example, inquiry-based learning , differentiation , and cooperative learning are strategies you likely included in your previous teaching, but may not have named on your resume. Address Career Gaps ‍ No need to pretend the gap didn’t happen or that you were spending that time gearing up for this role. Acknowledge the gap honestly and directly, but with a positive frame. For example, if you took a break from your career to care for a family member, you can list “Caregiver” with the dates under the Experience section of your resume. When summarizing your accomplishments in that role, refer to skills you improved such as people skills, budgeting and time management. No matter the reason for the gap, highlight the transferable skills you gained that will contribute to your success as a teacher. Research the Hiring Landscape ‍ Before you can start applying for teaching jobs, you need to explore what jobs are available and what type of school would be the best fit for you now. (Nimble Connect offers some tools , including a preferences quiz to help with this.) Once you have a school in mind, get clear on its mission, unique programming, demographics served and recent student performance. Check their website and social media pages to see what they highlight and how they celebrate their students. Customize Your Application ‍ If you’re presenting a cover letter or asked to respond to short essay questions, make sure everything you submit is unique to the specific position you’re applying for and the particular context of the school. Share the things about that school that attract you to it and showcase how your experience will positively impact the students and community you’d be working with. Prepare for the Hiring Process If it’s been a while since you’ve applied for a job, you’ll likely need some practice before you’re ready to present yourself confidently. Some of our other blog posts provide helpful tips on this front. You should spend some time speaking in front of a friend or even a mirror about your experience, your teaching philosophy, your aspirations and what makes you an excellent candidate for the role. Be prepared to speak to why you stepped away from teaching and why you’re coming back. It shouldn’t take long before your teacher voice returns and you’re ready to demonstrate your potential to a principal. You’ve Got This Schools are actively looking for experienced educators who bring both skill and fresh perspective. With the right preparation, you can return to teaching with clarity, purpose and confidence.

title: Is Your Pharmacy Staff Burned Out? 3 Workflow Fixes for 2026
summary: Three tips for pharmacy staff burnout.
body_text: Pharmacy staff burnout isn't a new phenomenon: about 62% of pharmacy professionals experience burnout. More than just a staffing headache for independent pharmacy owners, burnout drives errors, erodes patient relationships, and accelerates turnover in a market where finding qualified staff is already brutal. ‍ The good news: most burnout in community pharmacy isn't caused by people who are unhappy with their jobs. It's caused by workflows that weren't designed for the volume, complexity, or regulatory load they're now carrying. ‍ Why Pharmacy Burnout Has Become a Structural Problem ‍ Burnout in healthcare is typically tracked across three dimensions: emotional exhaustion, depersonalization (cynicism toward patients), and a reduced sense of personal accomplishment. ‍ The root causes can be largely operational: Understaffing: Independent pharmacies are routinely handling the same workload they once staffed for two or three more people. Cognitive overload: Pharmacists juggle clinical decisions, insurance rejections, patient counseling, prescriber communications, and inventory management simultaneously. Each task switch costs time and mental bandwidth. Administrative drag: Direct and Indirect Remuneration (DIR) fee reconciliations, prior authorizations, and documentation requirements consume hours that should go toward patient care. Interruption culture: Research in community pharmacy settings finds pharmacists face anywhere from 3 to 7 interruptions per hour , with some studies clocking nearly 6 per hour on average. Each one resets the cognitive clock. ‍ 3 Workflow Fixes That Actually Move the Needle ‍ Fix 1: Restructure the Prescription Queue to Reduce Cognitive Load ‍ The default "first in, first out" queue model is one of the biggest contributors to staff burnout because it treats every prescription as equal urgency. It isn't. ‍ A priority-tiered queue separates prescriptions into three buckets: ‍ Priority Description Target Turnaround Urgent Same-day fills, post-discharge, emergency refills Under 30 minutes Standard Regular maintenance fills with patient waiting 1–2 hours Scheduled Refills not yet picked up, blister packs, med sync End of day or next morning ‍ When staff aren't mentally triaging every incoming script on their own, decision fatigue drops sharply. Assign one team member per shift to own the queue structure rather than letting it pile up organically. ‍ Actionable step: Audit your queue process this week. If you don't have a written triage protocol, draft one using your three highest-volume prescription categories as the starting framework. ‍ Fix 2: Automate the Tasks That Are Burning Out Your Best People ‍ Repetitive, low-judgment tasks (refill reminders, pickup notifications, basic insurance verification follow-ups) are disproportionately demoralizing because they're time-consuming but don't require the skills your staff actually trained for. ‍ Automation doesn't mean replacing people. It means redirecting them toward work that requires clinical judgment and human connection. ‍ Tools like Nimble help independent pharmacies automate patient communications, refill workflows, and outreach without adding headcount. When a technician isn't spending 45 minutes per day on outbound reminder calls, that time goes back into patient care, managing prior auths, or simply leaving work on time. ‍ Specific workflows worth automating in 2026: Refill reminder texts and calls Ready-for-pickup notifications Adherence follow-ups for high-risk chronic disease patients Appointment reminders for vaccine or MTM services ‍ Pharmacies using automated patient engagement tools report saving 1 to 3 staff hours per day, which compounds fast across a calendar year. ‍ Actionable step: List every repeating communication task your team handles manually. Anything that follows a script and doesn't require clinical judgment is a candidate for automation. ‍ Fix 3: Build Micro-Boundaries Into the Shift Structure ‍ This one costs nothing but scheduling discipline, and it may be the highest-leverage fix of the three. ‍ Pharmacists and technicians in community settings rarely get uninterrupted time for focused work. The result is a phenomenon called attention residue, where incomplete tasks linger in working memory and compound cognitive load even when staff move on to other work. ‍ Structured micro-boundaries look like this: Protected processing windows: Designate 20-minute blocks (1-2 per shift) where one staff member handles the floor while others complete focused clinical or administrative tasks without interruption. Handoff protocols: Replace verbal status updates with a brief written shift handoff so outgoing staff aren't mentally carrying tasks into their personal time. "Not now" scripts: Train staff to use a short verbal redirect when interrupted during focused tasks: "I'm in the middle of a verification. Can you give me 5 minutes or grab [colleague]?" ‍ Small boundaries create psychological relief that accumulates shift by shift. ‍ Actionable step: Implement one 20-minute protected processing window per pharmacist per shift for the next two weeks. Measure whether error rates or end-of-shift stress levels change. ‍ Key Takeaways for Independent Pharmacy Owners 62% of pharmacy professionals reported burnout, pointing to a retention and safety crisis in the industry. Burnout in community pharmacy is primarily structural, driven by cognitive overload, administrative burden, and workflow inefficiency, not individual resilience failures. Tiered prescription queues reduce decision fatigue without adding staff or cost. Automating low-judgment, repetitive communication tasks (refill reminders, pickup notifications, adherence outreach) with tools like Nimble reclaims 1 to 3 hours of staff time daily. Micro-boundaries and protected focus time are free interventions with measurable impact on attention, error rates, and end-of-shift stress. ‍ Burned-out staff make more errors, leave faster, and cost more to replace than any workflow investment you'll make this year. The pharmacies that solve this operationally, not just culturally, will have a staffing and clinical quality advantage that compounds over time. ‍

title: The Mental Health Benefits of Pickleball for Older Adults
summary: From easing loneliness to sharpening the mind, research points to real mental health benefits of pickleball for older adults. Here's what the science says.
body_text: 5 Ways Pickleball Supports Well-Being Later in Life Most people take up pickleball for the exercise, but a growing body of research suggests its biggest payoff may be mental, and the benefits may be strongest later in life. It's built to help fight loneliness. In a 2025 national survey of 825 U.S. adults over the age of 50, published in the Journal of Primary Care & Community Health , those who had never played pickleball were about 1.5 times as likely as current players to report feeling lonely. Pickleball players, both current and former, also reported more social connections than those who never played. Part of it may be the court itself: at roughly 30% the size of a tennis court, it keeps players close enough to talk and laugh throughout a match. The more you play, the better you tend to feel. A 2025 study of 1,667 players in Frontiers in Psychology found a dose-response relationship between pickleball and mental well-being. Those who played three or more times a week, and for longer sessions, reported higher well-being scores. Notably, the effect was strongest among older adults, particularly those ages 63 to 77. A 2023 systematic review came to similar conclusions, associating pickleball with improvements in life satisfaction along with lower stress and symptoms of depression . It keeps the mind engaged. Pickleball asks a lot of the brain at once: tracking the ball, reading opponents, and adjusting shots quickly. Researchers call this kind of dynamic and reactive play open skill exercise, and a growing body of evidence suggests it may benefit the brain more than closed skill activities like running or swimming. While this research spans racquet sports broadly rather than pickleball specifically, it points to why a fast, strategic game may do more for the mind than a repetitive one. It can pull you into the moment. A 2026 study in the Journal of Aging and Physical Activity found that adults 60 and older who played recreational doubles pickleball reported stronger flow states, or feelings of total concentration and losing track of time, than other activities. Pickleball may offer a welcome mental break from the day's worries. It offers routine and a sense of purpose. Beyond the numbers, a 2025 qualitative study in the Journal of Positive Psychology and Wellbeing found that older pickleball players described the sport as a source of autonomy, purpose, and belonging, with many prioritizing community and connection over competition. A standing game gives the week a rhythm and something to look forward to, weaving movement and connection into everyday life rather than leaving them to chance. That kind of built-in structure can matter most in retirement , when the routines and relationships of work tend to fall away. Pickleball isn't a cure-all, or a replacement for mental health care , but perhaps the game itself was never really the point. What seems to keep people coming back is each other, and as we age, that connection is worth showing up for. If you or someone you love finds that connection isn't enough on its own, whether it’s low mood, anxiety, or something harder to name, evidence-based care may help. According to 2026 data , 73% of LifeStance patients* experienced improvement in depression symptoms and 79% in anxiety symptoms. *amongst 150,000 LifeStance patients with at least moderate depression and 140,000 with at least moderate anxiety

body_text: View all news Johnson & Johnson Announces a Proposed Resolution of Ovarian Talc Litigation 07/27/2026 Download (opens in new window) PDF 217 KB Follows Favorable Multi-District Litigation Court Causation Ruling and the Company’s Successful Strategy to Defend Each Case Efficient Conclusion to the Talc Litigation that Eliminates Expense Associated with Litigating Remaining Roughly 76,000 Ovarian Talc Claims NEW BRUNSWICK, N.J.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Johnson & Johnson (NYSE: JNJ) (the "Company") today announced that it has reached an agreement for a comprehensive resolution of the remaining talc litigation with the plaintiff firms leading the federal Multi-District Litigation (MDL) and related state court proceedings, conditioned on, among other things, the express participation of at least 95% of the remaining claims. The proposed resolution follows a favorable ruling by the MDL court, and acknowledgment by plaintiffs’ counsel, regarding plaintiffs’ inability to prove that the Company’s talc products caused any particular claimant’s ovarian cancer (“specific causation”). “After decades of litigation and full vetting of the science in an extensive hearing, plaintiffs effectively conceded their inability to prove specific causation by withdrawing their experts on the topic in two bellwether cases. In a watershed moment, the Court thereafter ordered plaintiffs to show why the remaining claims should not be dismissed, confirming what we have maintained for years: that these claims lack scientific merit and were sustained only by unreliable expert opinions that could not survive rigorous judicial review," said Erik Haas, Worldwide Vice President of Litigation, Johnson & Johnson. "The Court’s order placed plaintiffs in an untenable position of having to present specific causation evidence to maintain their claims that does not exist. While we are confident the Company would have ultimately prevailed with further litigation, as it has in the vast majority of cases tried to date, this resolution allows the Company to put this matter behind it and remain focused on its mission to develop medicines and devices that save lives." The MDL Court’s recent specific causation ruling confirmed the Company's longstanding position that these claims lack scientific merit. The Company has prevailed in the overwhelming majority of ovarian cases tried to date. On July 22, 2026, the MDL court ordered plaintiffs to show why the remaining pending talc claims should not be dismissed for inability to prove specific causation. The order followed plaintiffs’ withdrawal of their specific causation experts in two bellwether cases, after a hearing that demonstrated their opinions were not based upon reliable scientific methodologies. The developments affirmed the Company’s longstanding position that the talc claims are premised on junk science that has been rejected for decades by United States scientific organizations and regulatory agencies, as well as independent experts. The proposed resolution constitutes an efficient conclusion to the talc litigation. The resolution: Requires and is conditioned on—among other criteria—the participation of lead plaintiff firms in all ovarian talc litigation pending in state and federal court, representing at least 95% of the remaining claims. Calls for per claim payments, with a $5.5 billion commitment by the Company and the first payment of no more than $3 billion to be made in 2027 and no additional payments due before 2028. Complements the progress the Company already has made to resolve the talc litigation, including previously settling about 95% of filed mesothelioma lawsuits, all State consumer protection claims, and all talc-supplier disputes. Brings finality to this meritless 15-year litigation. Studies show talc is safe, does not contain asbestos and does not cause cancer. Research, clinical evidence, and decades of studies by independent medical experts around the world continue to support the safety of cosmetic talc. Prior to its separation, Johnson & Johnson agreed to retain all the talc-related liabilities and indemnify Kenvue for any and all costs—arising from litigation in the United States and Canada. As part of a worldwide portfolio assessment, Johnson & Johnson made the commercial decision to discontinue talc-based JOHNSON’S® Baby Powder globally in 2023. Additionally, Johnson & Johnson separated its consumer health business, Kenvue, in August 2023. Additional information on the Company's position and the science supporting the safety of talc is available at www.FactsAboutTalc.com . About Johnson & Johnson: At Johnson & Johnson, we believe health is everything. Our strength in healthcare innovation empowers us to build a world where complex diseases are prevented, treated, and cured, where treatments are smarter and less invasive, and solutions are personal. Through our expertise in Innovative Medicine and MedTech, we are uniquely positioned to innovate across the full spectrum of healthcare solutions today to deliver the breakthroughs of tomorrow and profoundly impact health for humanity. title: The 10 biomarkers that reveal your brain's terrain
summary: 10 markers that reflect your brain health, and how to measure them.
body_text: This listicle is inspired by our two-part series on cognitive health: Part 1: what cognitive health really means and Part 2: the pillars that support your brain . Faltering memory, fading focus, the end-of-day brain fog: these signals often reflect a shifting biological terrain. Here are 10 biomarkers that help you understand that terrain, and that you can act on. 1. Omega-3 index (EPA/DHA): the structure of your neurons DHA contributes to the structure of neuronal membranes, EPA to inflammatory modulation. Why it matters : well-built neuronal membranes support communication between neurons and synaptic plasticity. The omega-3 index lets you objectify your status rather than assume it. Context : A diet low in fatty fish Cognitive fatigue and brain fog Key takeaway : aim for 2 portions of fatty fish per week, or measure your omega-3 index to know where you stand. 2. Homocysteine: the methylation and vascular marker An amino acid regulated by vitamins B6, B9 and B12. Why it matters : elevated homocysteine may reflect a less favorable terrain for the brain, particularly in terms of vascular health and methylation. Context : Insufficient B vitamin intake A vascular terrain worth watching Key takeaway : it reads alongside B12 and folate. Discuss it with your doctor if elevated. 3. hs-CRP: the inflammation thermometer A marker of low-grade inflammation. Why it matters : when chronic inflammation persists, it can affect the brain through immune activation and oxidative stress. In the short term, this can translate into brain fog and harder concentration. Context : Brain fog, unusual fatigue Harder concentration Key takeaway : a chronic inflammatory terrain is worth identifying early. Review it with your doctor. 4. Fasting insulin / HOMA-IR (and HbA1c): the brain's energy The brain needs stable energy to think, remember and concentrate. Why it matters : when insulin resistance sets in, the brain's ability to use glucose efficiently can be impaired. HbA1c reflects blood sugar stability over time. Context : Brain fog after meals Cravings, need for sugar or caffeine Difficulty concentrating Key takeaway : stable blood sugar = a more stable brain terrain. Fasting insulin, HOMA-IR and HbA1c read together. 5. ApoB (advanced lipid panel): cerebral perfusion The brain depends on blood flow for its oxygen and nutrients. Why it matters : elevated ApoB and lipid metabolism disturbances can compromise cerebral perfusion over time. What protects the heart often protects the brain too. Context : A cardiovascular terrain worth watching Key takeaway : ApoB refines vascular risk assessment beyond classic cholesterol. 6. 25-OH vitamin D: support for repair A vitamin involved in repair and protection functions. Why it matters : vitamin D is among the nutrients that support the brain's repair, signaling and protection functions. Context : Often low status, especially in winter Key takeaway : easy to measure and correct. Have your 25-OH vitamin D tested. 7. Vitamin B12 and folate (B9): neurotransmitters and myelin Essential cofactors of brain function. Why it matters : B9 and B12 contribute to neurotransmitter synthesis, myelin and homocysteine regulation. Context : Mental fatigue, difficulty finding words Key takeaway : they read alongside homocysteine to assess the methylation terrain. 8. Ferritin: your iron stores Iron is a cofactor in the production of neurotransmitters. Why it matters : iron is among the cofactors needed to convert amino acids into neurotransmitters. Ferritin reflects your stores. Context : Fatigue, unstable mental energy Key takeaway : a simple marker, best interpreted alongside the inflammatory context. 9. Thyroid panel: the brain's tempo The thyroid influences brain energy and processing speed. Why it matters : a thyroid imbalance can translate into brain fog, lower concentration and cognitive fatigue. Context : Mental fatigue, slowness, lower concentration Key takeaway : a thyroid panel helps explain persistent cognitive fatigue. 10. Cortisol and DHEA-S: the stress axis Two key hormones of the stress response and recovery. Why it matters : cortisol modulates memory, stress and recovery. DHEA-S has documented neuroprotective effects and buffers some harmful effects of glucocorticoids. Context : Stronger emotional reactivity, slower recovery Unrefreshing sleep Key takeaway : cortisol and DHEA-S read together to assess stress load and resilience. Conclusion None of these markers alone diagnoses cognitive decline. Taken together, they answer a more useful question: is your brain operating in a terrain that supports mental clarity, repair and adaptation? At Lucis, we analyze these biomarkers in their full context, interpret your results and build a personalized plan adapted to your biological profile, not just "are you in range".
